provider: Scaleway (Iliad group) - Apple silicon Mac mini M4-S, bare metal dedicated (Apple M4 10C CPU / 10C GPU / 16 GB unified RAM / 256 GB SSD / 1 Gbps). Same-price-class alternative: M2-L (M2 Pro, 16 GB, 512 GB) EUR139/mo.
region_dc: PAR-1 (Paris / Saint-Ouen area, France) - only AZ listed for Apple silicon on the Scaleway pricing page
sovereignty_class: EU HQ (France) + EU DC = full EU sovereignty, no CLOUD Act exposure at the provider-corporate level. Scaleway holds ISO 27001 (and HDS for some products) at company level; SecNumCloud/BSI C5 NOT confirmed for Apple silicon product [uncertain]. Machine is Apple hardware running macOS (Apple MDM profiles present), so Apple remains a software-licence counterparty.
monthly_cost: EUR149/mo excl. VAT (M4-S 16GB) on monthly commitment = EUR149 24/7. Hourly price EUR0.22/h => ~EUR160/mo at 730h if left on hourly (24/7 hourly is dearer than commitment). POC-hours: 24h minimum lease = ~EUR5.28 per short test; 1 week ~EUR37. Optional Private Network EUR9.99/mo. Within the EUR150 budget only on the commitment price, excl. 20% French VAT (~EUR179 incl. VAT) [uncertain: VAT treatment depends on buyer status].
billing_granularity: Two modes: (a) monthly commitment, auto-renews monthly on anniversary, deletion takes effect on anniversary date; (b) hourly pay-as-you-go with mandatory 24h minimum lease (Apple macOS licence, section 3.A). Not scale-to-zero: billed while assigned until explicitly deleted. Cannot switch commitment -> hourly. If installed with Asahi Linux, no 24h minimum applies per FAQ.
setup_fee_and_lockin: No setup fee found on pricing page. Lock-in: 1 month initial commitment, auto-renewed monthly; exit = delete machine, effective at next anniversary (up to ~1 month of paid cost). Hourly route: 24h minimum (~EUR5.28). Exit cost otherwise zero except data migration. Egress/data stays on local 256 GB SSD.
gen_tps_7b_q4: ~18-22 t/s expected for Bielik-7B Q4_K_M (4.5 GB) [uncertain - bandwidth-derived/extrapolated, not measured on Scaleway]. Basis: llama.cpp maintainer benchmark (discussion #4167) Llama-2-7B Q4_0 (3.8 GB) on M4 10-core GPU, 120 GB/s: TG 24.11 t/s, PP512 221.29 t/s. Scaling by model size (3.8/4.5 GB) gives ~20 t/s; real-world with server overhead, long context ~15-20 t/s.
prefill_tps: ~170-220 t/s [uncertain - extrapolated]. Measured reference: M4 10-core Llama-2-7B Q4_0 PP512 = 221 t/s (Q8_0 224, F16 230). K-quants (Q4_K_M) typically a bit slower than Q4_0 on Metal, and PP degrades at long context, so planning figure ~150-200 t/s. The task-prompt estimate 80-150 t/s is conservative/pessimistic versus published M4 benchmark data. Not measured on Scaleway machine.
ttft_at_4k: ~20-27 s cold for a 4k-token prompt (4096 / 150-200 t/s) [uncertain - derived]; 8k tool schema ~40-55 s cold (attention cost makes it worse than linear). Mitigation: llama.cpp prompt/KV cache reuse (--cache-reuse, slot prompt caching) so static tool-schema prefix is only prefilled once; warm follow-ups then ~1-3 s. Poor for cold agentic bursts versus a GPU (L4: ~1-2 s).
concurrency_slots: Practically 1-2 slots. Bandwidth (120 GB/s) is shared, so aggregate decode does not scale; each extra slot divides ~20 t/s. KV cache for Mistral-7B-architecture (32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dim 128, f16): ~0.13 GB per 1k tokens (~131 KB/token) [uncertain - assumes Bielik-7B is Mistral-7B arch; can be halved with q8_0 KV]. e.g. -np 2 x 8k ctx = ~2.1 GB KV.
ctx_ram_headroom: 16 GB unified; macOS + services ~3-4 GB; Metal GPU working set default cap ~2/3-3/4 of RAM (~10.7-12 GB) [uncertain - default recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize, can be raised via sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb if permitted in MDM-managed host]. Model 4.5 GB + KV 0.13 GB/1k => 16k ctx ~2.1 GB (total ~7 GB, comfortable), 32k ctx ~4.2 GB (total ~9 GB, fits within cap). Native Bielik-7B context may be only 4k-8k (v0.1 = 4096; later versions larger) [uncertain]; long-context speed is limited by prefill, not RAM.
availability_status: Available on demand via console/CLI (PAR-1 listed with M4-S, M4-SP, M4-M, M4 Pro M4-XL). No waitlist found on pricing page; stock status not verifiable without account [uncertain].
egress_traffic: 1 Gbps public bandwidth listed (M4-M up to 10 Gbps). Scaleway Apple silicon pricing page lists no per-GB egress charge; Private Network option EUR9.99/mo unlimited up to 1 Gbps. Exact included traffic/overage terms not stated on page [uncertain]. One IPv4 + one IPv6 /128 per machine.
electricity_metering: Not applicable - fully managed bare metal, power included in monthly price, no per-kWh metering. For reference Mac mini M4 draws ~5-10 W idle, ~30-40 W under load.
hosting_model: Self-host llama.cpp (llama-server, Metal) on macOS via SSH/VNC - full control of GGUF, chat template (--jinja), tool-call parser, flags, context, slots. Bare environment preinstalled with Xcode, MacPorts; Homebrew/cmake can be installed. No managed API. Limitations: no recovery access, no SIP disable, no FileVault (MDM). Alternative: Asahi Linux image (no 24h minimum), but Metal/GPU compute under Asahi is not production-ready for llama.cpp (Vulkan only, partial) [uncertain].
tool_calling_support: Yes, via self-hosted llama-server OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with --jinja: server-side parser for tools when the model chat template supports it. Bielik has no official native tool-call template, so a custom Jinja template / generic tool handler (or grammar-constrained JSON) must be supplied and validated by operator. Full control of template/parser sits with the user.
spec_decode_support: Yes in principle: llama.cpp supports speculative decoding (--model-draft / -md) with a small draft model on Metal; a Bielik draft (DFlash or small distilled model) can be loaded. Memory headroom is fine (16 GB). Caveat: with 120 GB/s bandwidth and compute-limited GPU, gain is modest, and batched verification on a small M4 GPU may give limited speedup [uncertain].
sla_uptime: No GPU-grade SLA for Apple silicon identified; Scaleway compute SLAs usually ~99.9% for standard instances but Apple silicon-specific SLA not published on pricing/FAQ pages [uncertain]. Single physical machine, no redundancy, no live migration.
llm_inference_tos: No explicit prohibition on LLM inference found; Scaleway markets Mac mini M4 Pro for 'AI and machine learning' workloads (pricing page). Apple macOS SLA restricts leasing (24h minimum) but not workload type. Standard Scaleway AUP applies (no abuse). Not legally verified end-to-end [uncertain].
price_stability: Apple silicon prices have risen historically (task note: Scaleway Apple +45%) [uncertain - not independently verified here]. Current EUR149/mo M4-S; commitment renews monthly at then-current price [uncertain]; no price lock beyond month. Per note in task constraints, treat 6-month stability as moderate-risk.
model_lock_in: Low. Self-host: the model is a GGUF file chosen by operator; no managed catalog dependency, so Bielik cannot be removed from under you (unlike Scaleway Generative APIs / OVH AI Endpoints where Bielik was dropped). Lock-in is only to a 1-month commitment and to macOS/Metal; GGUF + llama.cpp is portable to any other host.
